text.autoconfig.aura-intro.title: Aura-Intro
text.autoconfig.aura-intro.option.genera: Master switch. When disabled the mod does nothing at all.
Fade wordmark in after the video
Keep the "MINECRAFT" wordmark hidden while the video plays and fade it in once the video has ended. Off leaves the wordmark exactly as vanilla draws it.
Fade wordmark in at the first loop

Only with the option above and LOOP_REGION. A loop never ends, so the wordmark would stay hidden for good: on fades it in the first time the video loops, when the menu music takes over. Off keeps it hidden while the loop plays (for a video with its own logo).
Hides the rotating yellow splash text.
Logs timing and video state changes - useful while tuning the timings.
Suppress menu music during the video
Keep Minecraft's menu music quiet while the video is playing, so it cannot talk over the video's own soundtrack. The music returns when the video has ended.
Play the whole video intro again whenever the loading splash appears (F3+T, resource pack changes).
Play the video that ships inside the mod when the configured file is missing - so the video works with no setup, and a file at that path takes over whenever there is one.
Video file
Path to the intro video, relative to the game directory. A file there overrides the video bundled with the mod; if it is missing, the bundled one plays.
Volume (%)
Playback volume of the video's audio track.
Play sound in the video player

One player has one clock, so picture and sound cannot drift and no delay is needed. On by default. The sound then shares the video's demux, though, so it can stutter while the game loads a resource pack - off gives the sound its own player, lined up with the Audio delay option.
Audio delay (ms)
Shifts a baked video's sound relative to its picture. Positive plays the sound later - the fix when the sound runs ahead of the picture.
Audio output device

Output device the video's sound plays through. Empty follows the system's default output - the same one the game's own sound uses. On Linux this is a sink name as shown by the desktop's audio widget (e.g. the name of your headphones); only when the system sound server is unreachable is it a Java Sound mixer name instead (the log lists them).
Audio latency compensation (ms)

Extra fine-tuning on top of the automatically measured sound latency (Linux sound server; Bluetooth headphones included). Positive delays the picture further - raise it if the video still runs ahead of the sound, lower it (negative) if the sound runs ahead. Usually 0.
Opacity (%)
Extra opacity multiplier on top of the video's own alpha channel, for both the loading screen and the intro.
Fit mode
How the video is fitted to the screen, for both the loading screen and the intro: COVER crops, CONTAIN letterboxes, STRETCH fills.
Max upload FPS
Upper bound for texture uploads per second, for both the loading screen and the intro. 0 = unlimited.
Hardware decoding

Decode the video on the GPU: D3D11VA on Windows, VideoToolbox on macOS, VAAPI (Intel/AMD) or NVDEC (NVIDIA) on Linux. Falls back to software decoding automatically when no working hardware decoder is found.
text.autoconfig.aura-intro.option.timing: How long the video fades in once it starts. Only used when the loading screen does not show the video.
Video timestamp at which the vanilla progress bar starts fading. The Mojang logo keeps showing.
How long the progress bar takes to disappear.
Video timestamp at which the loading overlay (Mojang logo) is unloaded. 0 = let vanilla handle it.
INSTANT removes the loading scene at the timestamp; VANILLA_FADE lets it cross-fade over two seconds underneath the video.
Video timestamp at which the title screen buttons start fading in.
Video timestamp at which the version/mod-count line, the splash text and the Realms badge start fading in. They are fully transparent before it.
How long those texts take to fade in. 0 makes them appear instantly.
How long the buttons take to fade in. 0 makes them appear instantly.
Fade duration used when the end behaviour is FADE_OUT_TO_PANORAMA.
What happens when the video ends: loop a region, fade back to the panorama, or freeze the last frame.
Start of the loop region (only used by LOOP_REGION).
End of the loop region (only used by LOOP_REGION). 0 = end of the video. The first time the video loops, its sound is muted and the vanilla menu music starts.

Only with "Keep loop as menu background". On: the loop keeps playing behind the other menus (options, world select, ...), blurred, where vanilla shows its panorama. Off: it pauses until the title screen is back. In a world it pauses either way.

Only used by LOOP_REGION. On: the loop region stays the title screen's background for good - leaving the title screen (another menu, a world) pauses it, and it carries on when you come back instead of the panorama. The video stays muted and the vanilla menu music plays. Off: leaving the title screen ends the video and the panorama takes over.
text.autoconfig.aura-intro.option.layout: Moves the title screen buttons down (positive) or up (negative) by this many GUI pixels.

GUI scale for the whole title screen (buttons, logo, splash, version and copyright text, Realms badge) without changing any other screen, with exactly the vanilla GUI scale behaviour: 0 is Auto (largest scale the window supports), 1-4 are fixed scales clamped to what the window supports. -1 (default) follows the regular GUI scale.
Ignore the button fade timings above and keep vanilla's two second fade.
text.autoconfig.aura-intro.option.loadin: Show video behind the loading bar
Draw the intro video behind the vanilla loading bar instead of the plain red background. Off keeps the loading screen vanilla; the video then only starts (and fades in) once loading has finished.
Timestamp in the video where the loading screen freezes on a frame and waits for the game to finish loading; the intro then continues from that exact frame. 0 plays the clip through.
Fade-in duration once the loading screen appears. 0 (the default) cuts straight to the video.
Hide the vanilla MOJANG STUDIOS logo while the video is showing, so the loading bar sits directly on the video.
Wait until the freeze frame is reached
Keep the loading screen up until the video has reached the freeze frame (or its end, when the freeze frame is 0), so the intro never starts from a frame the loading screen has not shown yet.
Safety net for the option above: continue loading after this long even if the video never gets there. 0 = wait forever.
